    America is building just 10% of the power lines it needs, experts warn

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1168 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • America's electricity needs are growing rapidly, but the nation's aging power grid is struggling to keep up.
    • Recent findings suggest that in a Policy Forum paper published in Science, energy policy researchers from Carnegie Mellon University and the University of California San Diego warn that the United States faces one of the world's most serious bottlenecks in electricity transmission.
    • America Is Building Just 10% of the Power Lines It Needs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    America's electricity needs are growing rapidly, but the nation's aging power grid is struggling to keep up. More electric vehicles, increased electricity use in heavy industry, and the explosive growth of data centers are driving demand higher, putting additional pressure on an infrastructure system that is already falling behind.

    Recent findings suggest that in a Policy Forum paper published in Science, energy policy researchers from Carnegie Mellon University and the University of California San Diego warn that the United States faces one of the world's most serious bottlenecks in electricity transmission. The problem could have major consequences for electricity prices, grid reliability, and the nation's economic future.

    America Is Building Just 10% of the Power Lines It Needs.

    Sources indicate that A major concern is the extremely slow pace of transmission construction. Over the past five years, the continental United States has added an average of only about 500 miles of high-voltage transmission lines annually. Research suggests the country needs approximately 5,000 miles each year to triple the size of its interregional transmission network by 2050 and accommodate future electricity demand.

    Sources indicate that that means the U.S. is building upcoming high-voltage transmission lines at just one-tenth of the estimated pace needed.

    High-voltage transmission lines serve as the highways of the electricity system, carrying large amounts of power over long distances from generating facilities to communities and businesses. Connecting regional grids allows electricity to flow more easily between areas, helping balance supply and demand when local power production falls short.

    Recent findings suggest that studies have shown that larger, better-connected electricity networks can reduce costs for consumers while also lowering the risk of catastrophic blackouts. When one region experiences a power shortage, electricity from another region can help keep the lights on.

    Despite these advantages, expanding the nation's transmission infrastructure has proved extraordinarily difficult.

    The Biggest Obstacle Isn't Technology.

    According to the researchers (Madeline Yozwiak, David G. Victor, and M. Granger Morgan), the main barriers to modernizing America's power grid are political and regulatory rather than technological.

    Responsibility for approving major transmission projects is divided among federal agencies, state governments, local authorities, and private companies. Each has its own priorities and interests, creating numerous opportunities for proposed power lines to be delayed or blocked.

    Existing electric utilities can also have financial reasons to resist stronger connections between regions. Greater competition from electricity suppliers elsewhere could weaken their influence over local markets, reducing the incentive to support projects that would benefit the broader electricity system.

    As a result, even transmission projects that could lower costs and improve reliability across the country can struggle to gain approval.

    Three Ways to Fix America's Power Grid Crisis.

    To address the growing shortfall, the researchers recommend a three-part strategy combining stronger government action, modern transmission technologies, international cooperation, and regulatory reform.

    1. Make better use of existing federal powers and advanced technologies.

    The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and the Department of Energy (DOE) already have legal authorities that could help move important transmission projects forward. The researchers argue that these agencies should use those powers more effectively, including identifying transmission corridors of national importance and addressing disputes that prevent projects from receiving state-level approval.

    Recent findings suggest that technological improvements could also dramatically increase the amount of electricity the grid can carry. One approach, known as reconductoring, involves replacing existing power line conductors with more advanced materials capable of transmitting more electricity without necessarily requiring entirely new routes.

    Other advances, including newer High-Voltage Direct Current (VSC-HVDC) systems, offer additional ways to move large amounts of electricity efficiently. The researchers suggest that modern transmission technologies could double or even triple capacity.

    Industry observers note that underground high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables offer another promising option. These systems can carry substantial amounts of electricity over long distances and could potentially be installed along existing highways and railroad corridors. Using these established routes could help avoid some of the land-use disputes and approval challenges that often delay conventional transmission projects.

    2. Learn from countries that have already overcome similar obstacles.

    The United States trails several international counterparts in building long-distance HVDC infrastructure and coordinating electricity transmission across regional and national boundaries.

    It has been revealed that other countries have demonstrated that large transmission projects can move forward despite complicated political approval processes. Some have also successfully deployed underground HVDC systems on a large scale.

    Industry observers note that rather than developing every solution independently, the researchers suggest that the U.S. should study these international experiences and adapt approaches that have already proved successful.

    Industry observers note that one proposal is to establish an international forum involving electricity regulators and other experts, potentially led by organizations such as the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC). Such a forum could help American policymakers identify effective regulatory practices, planning strategies, and technologies used elsewhere.

    3. Create a national commission to break the political deadlock.

    The researchers also recommend establishing a Presidential-Congressional Transmission Commission to address the political and regulatory conflicts that have slowed grid expansion for decades.

    Modeled on previous successful bipartisan commissions, the proposed group would bring together key stakeholders to negotiate difficult decisions and develop a coordinated strategy for reform.

    Its responsibilities would include recommending changes to state and federal laws, examining whether FERC should receive broader authority over the locations of upcoming transmission projects, and developing financial incentives for companies that lead new construction.

    The commission could also recommend financial rewards for communities that host transmission infrastructure, helping ensure that local residents share in the benefits of projects that serve larger regions.

    Why America's Power Grid Crisis Could Get Worse.

    The researchers emphasize that the underlying challenge is not a lack of engineering solutions. Instead, the country's divided decision-making system allows individual stakeholders to obstruct projects that could deliver substantial nationwide benefits.

    "The fundamental challenge isn't technical, it's jurisdictional. Authority is divided among federal, state, and private entities, each with distinct priorities. When every stakeholder possesses the power to say no, even high-value projects that benefit the entire nation struggle to move forward," the authors warn.

    Their assessment suggests that simply continuing with the existing system of overlapping regulations and fragmented authority will not be enough to meet America's growing electricity needs.

    Without meaningful changes to how transmission projects are planned, approved, and built, the United States risks a prolonged infrastructure shortfall. The researchers warn that failing to resolve these problems could weaken electricity reliability and inflict lasting damage on the national economy, even as demand for power continues to climb.

    Industry observers note that materials provided by College of Engineering, Carnegie Mellon University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that everything is Crab is a roguelite evolution game where you start off as a blob, needing to eat to upgrade yourself and learn to survive!
    • Industry observers note that the map itself is interesting, with areas of snow, rain, and desert.
    • When you evolve, you can pick one of three upgrades that appear, some of which help you eat faster or ones that change the way you look physically, or ones that upgrade evolutions you have previously made.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that everything is Crab is a roguelite evolution game where you start off as a blob, needing to eat to upgrade yourself and learn to survive! There are some base-level stats that you can start with, sometimes making you a bit more than a blob, but you'll still need to come a long way if you want to survive in the harsh world around you.

    Industry observers note that the map itself is interesting, with areas of snow, rain, and desert. These areas can affect your blob, freezing you or slowing you down as you move through the sand. There are some foods along the ground in the form of fruits, but mainly you can beat up smaller creatures and bugs so that you can eat their flesh. This fills up a bar at the bottom of the screen that then allows you to evolve!

    When you evolve, you can pick one of three upgrades that appear, some of which help you eat faster or ones that change the way you look physically, or ones that upgrade evolutions you have previously made. There are some that give you bigger attacks or change the way that you dash away. It's quite fun to see the combination that you end up with and how they all gel together. Though, these evolutions are worth reading through because sometimes they have less-than-desirable effects that pair with them.

    In a recent development, as you continue to grow and evolve in Everything is Crab, there is also a timeline on the top of the screen. This shows moments when bosses will appear, who will trap you in a giant fenced area. You will then need to beat up this boss, as they will continue to chase you around until you've died. One giant spider guy actually started dropping web pods that released more spiders - it was quite the undertaking! Defeating bosses does give you DNA strips, which can be used to re-roll your evolutions or to upgrade your evolutions so that they do double the increase that you want to pick.

    There are some areas that you can discover, represented by a question mark on your map. These little interaction points give you three options to choose from, primarily at tiny trees or at giant mushrooms, which change how you interact with mushrooms in other places on the map. There are also places where you can hide, though that wastes time!

    Slowly, through doing more and more of these runs, you will unlock new ways of playing, like different difficulties or starting points for your blob, which continue to make the game more interesting. I like the size and pacing of these runs, which do save, so you do not need to do them all at once. I do find that sometimes the UI overlaps itself on my mobile phone, which can be a little strange, but you are still able to read everything anyway.

    It has been revealed that download now! Everything is Crab.

    Recent findings suggest that nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history.     Industry News: Crusader Kings publishers Paradox announce CEO swap, say they're "in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges"

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have revealed plans to switch overlords early next year.
    • In a recent development, while the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a new figurehead in place as the calendars swap.
    • "My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have revealed plans to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

    In a recent development, while the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a new figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the manufacturer's long-term development as a member of the board".

    "My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the tech giant’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over.".

    In a recent development, "The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards new gaming experiences that last for decades".

    It has been revealed that lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he said.

    As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

    According to recent reports, the past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their major strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the company had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

    With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld presently in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a major map.

    #109411. 10 Games to Play While Waiting for GTA VI to Go on Sale

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1509 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    10 Games to Play While Waiting for GTA VI to Go on Sale

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After 13 years, Rockstar’s long awaited follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto VI, has finally arrived on Xbox and PlayStation consoles to widespread critical and financial acclaim, becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.
    • While millions of people are playing through GTA VI today, many are also holding off from playing the game until it goes on sale due its high price ranging from $80-$100 and massive file size of 212 GB, taking up a massive chunk of the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S internal storage.
    • For those gamers who are holding off on purchasing GTA VI until it goes on sale, here’s a list of 10 GTA VI-like titles they should check out in the meantime that are presently being sold at more affordable prices and balanced file sizes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After 13 years, Rockstar’s long awaited follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto VI, has finally arrived on Xbox and PlayStation consoles to widespread critical and financial acclaim, becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.

    While millions of people are playing through GTA VI today, many are also holding off from playing the game until it goes on sale due its high price ranging from $80-$100 and massive file size of 212 GB, taking up a massive chunk of the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S internal storage.

    For those gamers who are holding off on purchasing GTA VI until it goes on sale, here’s a list of 10 GTA VI-like titles they should check out in the meantime that are presently being sold at more affordable prices and balanced file sizes.

    Some people just enjoy Grand Theft Auto games for their comedy and freedom to sow chaos throughout cities and for people who enjoy that type of experience they should check out the FPS High on Life from the creators of Rick and Morty.

    Here, people play as a human as they wind up being teleported to the alien metropolis of Blim City to become an intergalactic bounty hunter with living guns called Gatlians guiding them to take down the G3 Cartel that intends on turning the entire human race into drugs.

    High on Life is as ridiculous and hilarious as it sounds, essentially being a perfect translation of Rick and Morty’s signature comedy style to video game form, and it will certainly give players many laughs as they wait for GTA VI to go on sale.

    Ever since Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, flying all kinds of aircraft has been an integral part of the GTA experience and for those who enjoy flying more than driving in the franchise, there’s no better game to check out while waiting for GTA VI sales than Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

    The latest entry in the long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is the most advanced publicly available flight simulator, allowing players to learn how to fly a wide variety of aircraft in first or third-person such as airships, gliders, hot air balloons, jets, and more.

    Not only that, but the game additionally allows players to fly any aircraft across the planet’s most famous natural and urban environments such as Zion National Park, Mount Fuji, London, and Miami which is what GTA VI’s Vice City is directly based on.

    Even more so than flying, driving has arguably been the defining factor of the GTA franchise with the series initially starting out as a top-down driving-focused game and if GTA fans wanted to check out the most advanced realistic racing game, then they’d have to play Forza Horizon 6.

    At the moment an Xbox Series X|S console exclusive, Forza Horizon 6 has players journey to the rural and urban streets of a stylised version of Tokyo as they strive to qualify for the Horizon Festival or simply drive around Japan’s wondrous landscapes using over 500 cars.

    There’s far more to do in Forza Horizon 6 than just driving around Japan as players can customize a massive estate filled with garages and custom tracks or players can customize public roads to use in multiplayer races.

    Some people may enjoy the GTA series for the driving, flying, or comedy but oftentimes people like those games for the freedom to cause chaos in any way they desire, with one game that offers a similar style of player freedom being Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster.

    An RE Engine remake of 2006’s Dead Rising, Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster follows the photojournalist Frank West as he sneaks his way into a Willamette, Colorado mall to cover a zombie outbreak only to get trapped in the mall and attempt to investigate the outbreak’s origins.

    While players can stick to completing the game’s many time limited narrative cases, players can instantly go about slaying zombies and psychopaths in any way they want by using practically anything found in the mall such as jugs of orange juice, CDs, katanas, potted plants, shopping carts, and more.

    If people want to experience a game with a similar story and setting to GTA VI, there are actually a few good games to choose from with one of the more underrated options being Hangar 13’s Mafia III.

    The first Mafia game to not be developed by series creator Illusion Softworks, Mafia III follows Vietnam War veteran turned crime lord Lincoln Clay in the U.S. gulf coast city of New Bordeaux as he sets out to avenge his adoptive father and brother after they were killed by the Marcano crime family.

    While Mafia III isn’t set in the present day, it still features a similarly enthralling and emotional story, one that tackles social complications of late 1960s America and features multiple different endings depending on Clay’s actions and choices during his campaign to take down the local mafia.

    When it comes to video games centered around crime, most people wouldn’t consider an entry from the war-focused Battlefield series to be one but in 2015, Visceral Games did just that by creating the crime and police centered Battlefield Hardline.

    Visceral’s final game ever released, Battlefield Hardline’s campaign follows Miami Police Detective Nick Mendoza attempting to take down drug dealers and suppliers in the Florida based city only to discover corruption in the MPD and wind up being framed for a crime he didn’t commit.

    Hardline may not have been the game traditional Battlefield fans wanted at the time of its release but Visceral’s writing and gameplay prowess managed to make it stand as not only one of the most unique Battlefield games but also one of the most intriguing and cinematic.

    Ubisoft is famous for creating immersive open-world titles like the numerous entries from the Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry series but it wasn’t until 2014 that the publisher decided to make a more grounded GTA-like experience with Watch Dogs.

    Set in Chicago and the same universe as the Assassin’s Creed franchise, Watch Dogs follows hacker Aiden Pearce who, after a heist goes wrong, sets out to find the people responsible for putting a hit on him resulting in the death of his niece Lena.

    What ensues is an action-packed yet stealthy gaming experience as Pearce is able to hack particularly every piece of technology in the city from cellphones to trains and construction equipment to aid him in tracking his enemies down in between instances where Pearce has to steal cars or engage in gun fights.

    While Mafia III and Watch Dogs are fun GTA-like titles, neither of them compare to the pure chaos and drama that can be unleashed in CD Projekt Red’s ambitious first-person, open-world, action RPG Cyberpunk 2077.

    The latest brand-new game developed by the makers of The Witcher game series, Cyberpunk 2077 has players embody the cyborg mercenary V in the futuristic and crime-filled metropolis of Night City as they get caught up in a movement to take down the corrupt Arasaka Corporation.

    Cyberpunk 2077’s reputation may have been marred by a buggy 2020 launch but it has since gone on to become one of the best modern RPGs thanks to beneficial updates and its Phantom Liberty DLC making the game’s core combat, dialogue, and side activities all the more fun.

    GTA VI is set in the present day but its greatest gaming influence on a technical and narrative level is undoubtedly Rockstar Games’ previous modern gaming major hit, Red Dead Redemption 2.

    Set roughly 12 years before Red Dead Redemption 1 at the turn of the 20th century, Red Dead Redemption 2 primarily follows Van der Linde gang member Arthur Morgan as he and the rest of the gang struggle to survive against rival gangs, nature itself, and the ever-dominating presence of industrialized civilization.

    Before GTA VI, Red Dead Redemption 2 was Rockstar’s most cinematic and immersive game ever made as not only did it feature a far more serious and emotional story than any GTA game before but it allowed players to do all kinds of things in the old west such as hunting wildlife, taking care of horses, crafting materials, and more.

    For anybody still waiting on GTA VI or consoles with large internal storage capacities to go on sale, the number one game they have to play in the meantime is the multi console generational juggernaut itself, GTA V.

    GTA VI is making records now but GTA V was a phenomenon all on its own for over a decade as it constantly outsold almost every other game on the market for years on end partly due to its campaign following Franklin, Michael, and Trevor in Los Santos but mainly due to its ever evolving GTA Online.

    With GTA VI’s iteration of GTA Online likely months away from launch, it’ll be good to finish up whatever players haven’t done yet in GTA Online, such as its many heists and mode customization options, before everyone migrates over to GTA VI’s multiplayer.

    The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an revision on what to expect in 2026

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of latest content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
    • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.
    • Recent findings suggest that the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of latest content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

    The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one upgrade on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

    In a recent development, in the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of problems should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

    The first stage of the upcoming roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

    According to recent reports, the infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo complications, and other crashes and freezing.

    Recent findings suggest that the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

    Recent findings suggest that another vital area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

    Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

    In a recent development, the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

    Sources indicate that until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

    #109409. Breaking: A simple metal is hiding a strange fresh form of magnetism

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1594 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: A simple metal is hiding a strange fresh form of magnetism

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A surprisingly simple metal has revealed an unusual form of magnetism that could open latest possibilities for quantum technology.
    • The material, known as europium silicide (EuSi), contains an intricate magnetic structure that influences how electrons move and how their spins are oriented.
    • The discovery is particularly significant because EuSi is a relatively simple metallic compound.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A surprisingly simple metal has revealed an unusual form of magnetism that could open latest possibilities for quantum technology. Researchers have found compelling evidence of a rare magnetic state in which electrons behave in unexpected ways, even though the material produces no overall magnetization.

    The material, known as europium silicide (EuSi), contains an intricate magnetic structure that influences how electrons move and how their spins are oriented. This behavior is associated with a phenomenon called p-wave magnetism, an emerging area of research that could eventually help scientists develop new approaches to controlling electronic properties.

    The discovery is particularly significant because EuSi is a relatively simple metallic compound. Unlike many materials previously considered for studying this exotic form of magnetism, it offers researchers a practical way to investigate the underlying physics in detail.

    An Unexpected Discovery in a Simple Metal.

    Recent findings suggest that the research began about three years ago at the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids (MPI CPfS) in Dresden, Germany. Dr. Erjian Cheng successfully grew high-quality single crystals of EuSi, providing the material needed for detailed experiments.

    It has been revealed that when researchers first examined the crystals using photoemission techniques, which probe the energies and behavior of electrons inside materials, they noticed something unexpected. The magnetic arrangement of the atoms had a remarkably strong influence on the electronic band structure, which describes the energy levels electrons can occupy and helps determine how a material conducts electricity.

    In a recent development, that observation raised an intriguing possibility. Could this simple compound contain an unconventional form of magnetism in which the spin of an electron is connected to the direction it travels?

    Sources indicate that "When we first measured the electronic structure of EuSi, we were surprised by the exceptionally large effect of magnetism on the electrons," explains Cheng. "That observation led us to investigate whether this simple compound could host a much more unusual magnetic state. The combination of crystal growth, neutron scattering and spin-resolved spectroscopy now provides compelling evidence for p-wave magnetism.".

    It has been revealed that answering that question required an international collaboration involving 38 scientists from 19 institutions. Participants included researchers from ShanghaiTech University, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, the Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems and Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

    A Strange Form of Magnetism That Cancels Itself Out.

    It has been revealed that ordinary magnets, such as those attached to refrigerators, typically rely on a magnetic arrangement called ferromagnetism. In these materials, many electron spins align in the same direction, producing an overall magnetic field.

    At temperatures between approximately 33 and 62 kelvin, the magnetic moments of its europium atoms organize themselves into a repeating spiral pattern. These temperatures correspond to roughly minus 400 to minus 348 degrees Fahrenheit.

    In a recent development, each europium atom has a substantial magnetic moment, but their orientations balance one another across the spiral. As a result, the material has no net magnetization in this magnetic phase.

    Recent findings suggest that however, the absence of overall magnetization does not mean magnetism has stopped influencing the electrons. In fact, the researchers found that the spiral arrangement produces a highly unusual electronic structure.

    In the proposed p-wave magnetic state, electrons traveling in opposite directions have opposite spin polarizations. Electron spin is a quantum property that gives electrons magnetic characteristics, although it should not be understood as an electron literally spinning like a tiny ball.

    In a recent development, the relationship between an electron's direction of motion and its spin is called an odd-parity spin texture. This means that reversing the electron's momentum also reverses the associated spin polarization.

    Other materials can display spin-dependent energy differences because of a phenomenon known as spin-orbit coupling, which connects an electron's motion to its spin. In EuSi, however, the unusual spin structure appears to arise mainly from interactions between magnetic moments and the specific symmetry of their spiral arrangement.

    Experiments Reveal Evidence of Rare P-Wave Magnetism.

    To determine whether EuSi truly exhibits the predicted magnetic state, the scientists combined several sophisticated experimental methods with theoretical calculations.

    Industry observers note that first, they used neutron diffraction, a technique that reveals how atoms and magnetic moments are arranged inside a material. These measurements confirmed that the europium magnetic moments form a spiral structure with the symmetry required for p-wave magnetism.

    Next, the researchers examined the material using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. This method measures the energies and momenta of electrons, allowing scientists to map the electronic structure.

    Industry observers note that the results showed that magnetic ordering substantially reorganizes the electron energy levels. In particular, the team observed magnetically driven energy separations exceeding 100 millielectronvolts, indicating an unusually strong influence of magnetism on electron behavior.

    The most decisive evidence came from spin-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which allowed the researchers to examine electron spin polarization directly.

    They observed that the sign of the spin polarization changed across successive magnetic Brillouin zones. These zones are regions of momentum space used by physicists to describe how electrons behave within a repeating magnetic structure.

    The team also found that spin polarization became much weaker near locations where theoretical calculations predicted the p-wave spin texture should disappear.

    Taken together, the measurements provide compelling experimental evidence consistent with the predicted p-wave magnetic state in EuSi.

    A Hidden Magnetic Spiral With Two Different Orientations.

    The researchers uncovered another unusual feature of EuSi involving chirality, a scientific term describing handedness.

    A familiar example is the difference between a left hand and a right hand. They are mirror images, but they cannot be perfectly superimposed.

    It has been revealed that something similar happens with the magnetic spiral inside EuSi. Although the underlying crystal has a centrosymmetric structure, meaning its atomic arrangement is unchanged by inversion through a central point, the magnetic spiral can twist in either of two opposite directions.

    These different spiral orientations create magnetic regions, or domains, with opposite handedness.

    Using magnetic force microscopy and spatially resolved photoemission spectroscopy, the scientists identified domains measuring approximately ten micrometers across. For perspective, ten micrometers is about one-tenth the thickness of a typical human hair.

    When the researchers examined these regions using circularly polarized light, they detected different electronic responses depending on the handedness of the magnetic spiral.

    This finding demonstrates that the direction in which the magnetic structure twists is linked to the material's electronic properties.

    It has been revealed that "What makes EuSi particularly exciting is that an unconventional electronic spin structure emerges from the magnetic order of a chemically simple metal," indicates Prof. Claudia Felser, Director at MPI CPfS. "This demonstrates how the discovery of new materials can reveal entirely new electronic phenomena. EuSi now gives us an experimental platform to investigate how magnetic symmetry and chirality can be used to control electronic properties, with potential implications for future spintronics and unconventional superconductivity.".

    Why This Discovery Matters for Quantum Technology.

    One of the biggest challenges in studying p-wave magnetism has been finding materials that display the necessary magnetic properties while remaining practical for detailed experiments.

    Earlier candidates have included insulating materials, as well as metals that develop the required magnetic order only at extremely low temperatures or have complicated symmetries that make their behavior difficult to interpret.

    EuSi offers a particularly useful combination of characteristics.

    It is a stoichiometric metal, meaning its constituent elements occur in a fixed chemical ratio. Researchers can also grow high-quality single crystals of the material, and its spiral magnetic arrangement has the symmetry associated with p-wave magnetism.

    Together, these features make EuSi a promising experimental platform for exploring how exotic magnetic states influence the behavior of electrons.

    According to recent reports, theoretical studies suggest that metallic p-wave magnets could display several remarkable properties. For example, they may allow electrons with particular spin orientations to carry electrical currents without requiring an external magnetic field.

    They could also produce strong changes in spin polarization when an electric current is applied, potentially offering upcoming ways to manipulate electronic behavior.

    These possibilities are especially relevant to spintronics, a field of technology that seeks to use electron spin, rather than electrical charge alone, to process and store information.

    Another intriguing possibility involves unconventional superconductivity, in which electrical current flows without resistance through superconducting states that differ from those found in conventional superconductors.

    According to recent reports, importantly, these predicted effects have not yet been demonstrated in EuSi. The discovery does not establish that the material can already perform these functions, but it gives researchers a promising system in which to test the predictions.

    More broadly, the findings highlight how much of a material's behavior can remain hidden beneath an apparently simple chemical composition.

    A solid's properties depend on more than the elements it contains or how its atoms are positioned. The arrangement of magnetic moments, the symmetries they create, and the quantum behavior of electrons can also produce entirely unexpected effects.

    By revealing compelling evidence of p-wave magnetism in EuSi, researchers have gained a latest opportunity to investigate these relationships and explore how unusual magnetic structures might eventually be used to control the electronic properties of future materials.

    Materials provided by Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    #109407. The Rings of Power season 3 episode 7 director breaks down the "huge pressure" of forging the One Ring for the first time on screen

    The Rings of Power season 3 episode 7 director breaks down the "huge pressure" of forging the One Ring for the first time on screen

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Rings of Power season 3 has now aired its most dramatic moment yet: the forging of the One Ring.
    • Creating the sequence was the culmination of years of work for The Rings of Power showrunners JD Payne and Patrick McKay, and for the episode's director, Stefan Schwartz, bringing it to screen for the first time came with "huge pressure".
    • According to recent reports, "You've got so many massive Rings fans and it's tricky because there's nothing in any of the books that describe how the Ring was created, and we scoured everything to try and glean any little bits and pieces," he tells GamesRadar+.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Rings of Power season 3 has now aired its most dramatic moment yet: the forging of the One Ring. In episode 7, Sauron enters Mount Doom and gives everything he has to create the ultimate weapon in his quest for power in Middle-earth.

    Creating the sequence was the culmination of years of work for The Rings of Power showrunners JD Payne and Patrick McKay, and for the episode's director, Stefan Schwartz, bringing it to screen for the first time came with "huge pressure".

    According to recent reports, "You've got so many massive Rings fans and it's tricky because there's nothing in any of the books that describe how the Ring was created, and we scoured everything to try and glean any little bits and pieces," he tells GamesRadar+. "So really approaching that scene, we had to create a whole bunch of upcoming thoughts.".

    Industry observers note that for Schwartz, a lot of this came down to making sure the sequence was magical, and really represented the world that Tolkien created. One element of that was imagining that the One Ring was created by the vibrations of Fëanor's hammer in Mount Doom, rather than simply being forged.

    "I wanted Mount Doom to be a real character and actually to work with him rather than just be a place where he happens to be," he explains. "At [Middle-earth's] very inception, a song was created, and then a little bit of darkness was introduced by the song through one of the characters, and then this song created Middle-earth. That music felt really key, and Tom Bombadil is always singing, it seems key to Tolkien's world. So I wanted the idea of music and vibration to be in there.".

    Recent findings suggest that another interesting addition to the sequence is how Sauron ends up giving his life to creating the One Ring, before it brings him back. Schwartz stated they wanted to play with the audience a bit here too. "The other key moment for all of us was sacrifice, that Sauron has to basically give up his life in order to create the ring, and then the ring brings back his life," he adds. "That moment of death and utter silence was really vital.".

    The final sequence is undoubtedly the show's most cinematic moment yet, and it's little wonder they wanted to bring it to theaters for a special screening. However, beyond spectacle, it seems that, above all, those involved wanted to do justice to the world that Tolkien created.

    Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

    "When you've got such an avid fan base, you want to try and be as true as you can be to the lore," Schwartz sums it up. "And then work within that and try to get elements that feel intuitive and connected to if Tolkien had created it, what he might have created.".

    Fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

    Sources indicate that fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

    Sources indicate that the club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that his next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

    According to recent reports, the rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that that deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

    In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

    It has been revealed that the overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

    Sources indicate that A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

    The club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert indicates Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The latest hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

    Recent findings suggest that I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

    Recent findings suggest that worst Class Ever is a upcoming don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

    Recent findings suggest that all of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

    Sources indicate that what a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

    #109402. Tech Report: While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (564 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones.
    • Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
    • Industry observers note that still, it’s clever with its limitations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

    Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

    Industry observers note that still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

    According to recent reports, which is welcome, as these significant lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

    Industry observers note that recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

    I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

    #109400. Tech Report: Cannabis owners develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1641 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Cannabis owners develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug.
    • Recent findings suggest that the findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney.
    • In a recent development, psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug. Even more concerning, the difference becomes substantially larger with age, reaching more than six years among people who develop psychosis in their 30s or later.

    Recent findings suggest that the findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney. They suggest that the potential psychiatric consequences of cannabis use may extend well beyond adolescence and could become more pronounced with prolonged exposure.

    In a recent development, psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations, false beliefs known as delusions, and disturbances in thinking or behavior. It can occur in schizophrenia and several other mental health disorders. Although psychosis most commonly begins during the late teenage years or early adulthood, it can develop at other stages of life. According to Psychosis Australia, up to 3% of adults will experience a diagnosed disorder involving psychosis during their lifetime.

    Cannabis Linked to Earlier Psychosis Across Adulthood.

    To investigate the relationship between cannabis use and the timing of psychosis, researchers at UNSW Medicine analyzed 149 studies involving more than 71,000 participants. Most of the research had been conducted since 2011 in Europe, North America, and Australia, with the majority of studies focusing on people diagnosed with schizophrenia.

    The researchers discovered that the difference in the age at which psychosis first appeared varied considerably across age groups.

    According to recent reports, in studies where the average age of psychosis onset was between 20 and 24, cannabis customers experienced their first episode approximately 1.6 years earlier than non-users. That difference widened to 4.43 years in studies involving people whose psychosis emerged in their mid-to-late 20s (25-29).

    Industry observers note that the largest difference appeared in studies where psychosis developed at age 30 or later. In this group, cannabis users experienced the condition an average of 6.3 years earlier than non-users.

    These results suggest that the association between cannabis and earlier psychosis may become stronger as people grow older, potentially reflecting the effects of longer periods of cannabis exposure.

    Why Cannabis Risks May Increase With Age.

    Chief investigator Matthew Large, a psychiatrist and Conjoint Professor at UNSW's School of Clinical Medicine, said the findings raise key questions about the long-term psychiatric effects of cannabis.

    Recent findings suggest that "We've tended to focus on the dangers of using cannabis in adolescence, when the brain is still developing, but the risk doesn't disappear once you're in your 20s," Prof. Large noted. "What we're seeing suggests a cumulative effect, where harm builds up over time, a bit like alcohol or nicotine.".

    Interestingly, the analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in the timing of psychosis between teenage cannabis people and teenagers who did not use cannabis.

    Sources indicate that however, the researchers cautioned that this finding does not necessarily mean younger cannabis users face no risk. Psychosis rarely develops before the middle teenage years, leaving relatively little opportunity for its onset to shift to an even younger age.

    According to recent reports, "There may be a biological floor, in that there is only so much earlier that onset can be shifted. In younger groups, strong development, genetic or other psychosis risk factors may dominate, making any cannabis-related age shift harder to detect," Prof. Large remarked.

    In a recent development, the researchers also stressed an crucial limitation. Because the analysis examined existing observational studies, it cannot establish that cannabis directly causes psychosis or makes the condition begin sooner. Demonstrating such a relationship experimentally would require research that deliberately exposed people to potential psychiatric harm, which would be unethical.

    It has been revealed that nevertheless, Prof. Large believes the overall pattern provides meaningful evidence supporting a possible causal connection.

    "But the consistency of the evidence, particularly the strong effect in older adults who likely have been using cannabis for longer, does support the theory that cannabis plays a causal role in the timing of psychosis onset, and possibly the onset of some cases among people who would not have otherwise developed psychosis.".

    New Findings Challenge Assumptions About Cannabis After Age 25.

    The latest research builds on two earlier investigations into cannabis use and the development of psychosis.

    Recent findings suggest that in a smaller 2011 meta-analysis led by Prof. Large, researchers found that psychosis began approximately 2.7 years earlier among cannabis users. A separate 2015 analysis reported that psychosis typically developed 6.3 years after cannabis use began.

    However, neither earlier investigation had enough information to determine how the relationship differed across age groups.

    By incorporating a much larger body of research, the latest analysis allowed scientists to examine how the association changes across different stages of adulthood.

    Lead author Carly Stevens, from UNSW's School of Biomedical Sciences, remarked the findings undermine the idea that avoiding cannabis during adolescence is sufficient to eliminate its potential psychiatric dangers.

    "What we've found challenges the assumption that you'll be fine if you wait to smoke weed until your mid-20s; that's just not the case," Ms. Stevens said.

    "There's been so much emphasis on adolescents not smoking cannabis, which is important, but we need to broaden the warnings for everyone.".

    Why Even a Few Years of Delayed Psychosis Matter.

    Although a difference of two or three years might initially seem relatively small, the researchers emphasized that the timing of psychosis can have profound consequences for a person's future.

    The late teenage years and early adulthood are often periods when people complete their education, begin careers, establish relationships, and develop greater independence. Experiencing a serious psychiatric disorder earlier in life can interrupt these key milestones.

    According to recent reports, "People may miss out on study, job opportunities, travel, and relationships in those years, and treatment can come with physical side effects that can make life harder as well," Ms. Stevens mentioned.

    Prof. Large emphasized the potential benefits of reducing or discontinuing cannabis use and the importance of delaying the onset of psychosis wherever possible.

    "It's a major illness, which robs you of your shared reality with family, friends and all those around you," he remarked. "If we can delay psychosis by even a few years, people will be more likely to reach crucial milestones in education and training, and develop strong support networks, which can protect against psychosocial decline.".

    It has been revealed that the potential benefits could also extend to healthcare systems. According to Prof. Large, psychotic disorders account for as much as 3% of health-related spending in developed countries. Preventing or delaying the onset of these conditions could therefore have substantial social and economic benefits.

    Scientists Call for Stronger Cannabis Health Warnings.

    Despite the inability to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship, the researchers believe their findings provide sufficient justification for stronger warnings about the possible psychiatric consequences of cannabis use.

    Sources indicate that "We can't run direct experiments, so we have to go with the best evidence available," Prof. Large stated. "In my view, the threshold for health warnings about cannabis and psychosis has definitely been met.".

    It has been revealed that one concern is the growing popularity of medical cannabis. Prof. Large noted its increasing use as a therapeutic product may encourage some people to assume that it carries little risk.

    He has also observed an increasing number of patients receiving treatment for psychosis who had previously been prescribed cannabis for medical conditions where evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited.

    "It's got this therapeutic halo around it, which blinds people to the risk.".

    Industry observers note that another emerging concern involves cannabis edibles, which can contain elevated concentrations of Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main compound responsible for the drug's mind altering effects. The availability of products containing higher THC concentrations raises additional questions about possible psychiatric risks.

    Recent findings suggest that at the same time, Prof. Large acknowledged that cannabis legalization could create opportunities to reduce harm, even though it would also make cannabis easier to obtain.

    Legal regulation could allow governments to establish limits on product potency, improve consumer education, introduce taxation, and require buyers to receive clear information about potential health consequences.

    "You could tax it, regulate it, and require people to show they understand the risks before buying," Prof. Large remarked.

    More Research Needed on Long-Term Cannabis Exposure.

    The researchers say further studies are necessary to understand the biological processes that might explain why the association between cannabis use and earlier psychosis becomes more pronounced with age.

    In particular, they want to investigate whether repeated or prolonged cannabis exposure produces cumulative changes that influence when psychotic symptoms emerge.

    They also recommend additional research focusing on older cannabis users, an increasingly important population as medical cannabis becomes more common and products containing high concentrations of THC become more widely available.

    According to recent reports, another priority is improving how cannabis exposure is measured. The researchers argue that future studies need clearer and more consistent methods for recording cannabis consumption so that findings can be compared more reliably.

    Ultimately, the new analysis highlights an key gap in public understanding of cannabis and mental health. While warnings have traditionally concentrated on teenage use, the findings suggest that potential psychiatric risks deserve attention throughout adulthood, particularly among people who continue using cannabis over many years.

    GTA 6: How to Find the Secret Satan Boss

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (675 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida.
    • One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight.
    • Sources indicate that if you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida. Some examples include the Kraken deep underwater, UFOs, and even a Mario and Luigi reference.

    One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight. Not only is it a really trippy mission, but it also rewards the player with one of the best weapons in the game.

    Sources indicate that if you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the secret Satan boss fight in GTA 6.

    To find the secret Satan boss in GTA 6, you must travel to the northern side of Port Gellhorn and visit the house with “Welcome to the Hellhole!” written on it. You can find the exact location of this house in the image of Port Gellhorn below.

    When you arrive at this house, the garage will either be open or closed. The Satan boss fight event can only be triggered if the garage is open, so if it happens to be shut when you arrive, then you’ll have to come back another time. This event all comes down to RNG, but there are ways to increase your chances.

    According to recent reports, first, the garage has a higher chance of being open late at night. For example, it was open for me around 10:00 PM, so I recommend only visiting the Hellhole house around this time.

    Industry observers note that keep in mind that the event won’t trigger if you just wait outside the house. Instead, I recommend using the RydeMe app to fast travel to another location and back to the house multiple times until the garage opens. This worked for me after five attempts.

    Once the garage finally opens, walk inside to find two men having some drinks. They will ask you if you want a beer, which you should grab from the cooler next to the couch.

    Recent findings suggest that for the next couple of minutes, make sure you don’t do anything to piss these guys off. You can talk to them, but don’t choose the “provoke” dialogue option or throw a bottle to mess up the event. Instead, wait patiently until their van arrives.

    According to recent reports, when the van arrives, the men will ask you to join them for their upcoming ritual. You should agree here and climb into the back of the van, which will then transport you to another location with a bonfire.

    Next, get out of the van and make your way to the bonfire to celebrate with the two Satanists, and wait until they tell you to look into the fire. Once the prompt “look into the fire” pops up, hold down the button to do just that.

    Looking into the fire will teleport you to hell, where you’ll have to fight a wave of Satan’s demons and Satan himself.

    Satan is not very difficult to defeat, but the fight can be a bit confusing. What you want to do here is shoot the exploding enemies that are running toward you, which will turn Satan’s health bar red.

    Once the health bar is red, you want to shoot at Satan to drain his health. When the health bar turns back to black, you want to repeat the process and kill the surrounding enemies to turn the bar red again.

    In a recent development, doing this a few times will have Satan going down fairly rapidly. Once you kill Satan, you will teleport back to the real world.

    Industry observers note that when players respawn back to the real world after fighting Satan in GTA 6, they will be granted a permanent health increase. Additionally, they’ll be able to claim the Hellspawn Cumshot 12 Shotgun next to the large throne.

    This shotgun is extremely powerful and is one of the best guns I have found in the game so far, so I recommend equipping it for any upcoming missions you have.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
    • HoYoverse declared last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
    • According to recent reports, the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

    HoYoverse declared last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

    According to recent reports, the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

    In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

    Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

    And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's enhancement.

    Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.
