    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Rings of Power season 3 ending is a surprising one, as the Dark Lord Sauron's last move of this installment is something you probably weren't expecting.

    In episode 7, he finally forged the One Ring, which means his victory was seemingly at hand as Númenor and the Elves gathered to stop him. The main action of the episode, however, is reserved for Gandalf and the Blue Wizard Pallando. Below, we break down all the twists and turns of the episode, so you can get up to speed at a glance.

    Sources indicate that that means there are spoilers ahead, so turn back now if you're not up to date. For everything you need to know about The Rings of Power season 3 ending, head to the below.

    In a recent development, the Rings of Power season 3 ending kicks off with the armies of Númenor and the Elves about to face Sauron's army of Orcs and men in battle. Sauron has the Blue Wizard Pallando on his side, and, of course, the Dark Lord just finished forging the infamous One Ring to Rule Them All.

    Sources indicate that yet all is not smooth sailing for Sauron. Gandalf proves impossible to corrupt, even after Sauron tries to trick him with a vision of his old Harfoot pal Nori. Meanwhile, Galadriel introduces Celeborn to Elrond and Gil-galad, and Pharazôn decides to fight Sauron despite the terrifying size of the Dark Lord's army.

    Recent findings suggest that sauron gifts Pallando a ring and makes a reference to the wizard becoming the Witch-king. However, it seems this is not Pallando's fate, as Gandalf is able to slip the ring from Pallando's finger and return his old friend to the light side. Sadly, Pallando is stabbed through the chest – though the wizard is able to survive long enough to help Gandalf get rid of Khamûl. Pallando's death spurs the men from Rhûn to abandon the fight.

    Recent findings suggest that gandalf then encounters Tom Bombadil, who is not tempted by Pallando's ring at all. In fact, he takes it from Gandalf and makes it disappear, then declines Gandalf's offer of his hat. Classic Tom.

    Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

    Sources indicate that finally, Theo warns Sauron that their forces are now evenly matched with the opposing side's, and Sauron reads a letter from Pharazôn gloating that Númenor is the "king of men." Bizarrely, Sauron chooses to surrender. While Pharazôn laughs heartily, relishing his victory, Gil-galad, Galadriel, and Elrond are more doubtful. The season ends with Sauron smirking, as his theme music plays ominously in the background.

    It has been revealed that there is only one significant death in The Rings of Power season 3 finale: Pallando. He is stabbed through the chest by a Nazgnagôl, but he dies redeemed. His death makes the forces of Rhûn abandon the incoming war, which turns the tide in favor of the Elves and Númenor. Also killed in this episode is Khamûl, the Nazgnagôl who snared Pallando to Sauron's side in the first place.

    Sauron tells Pallando that he could become "a Witch-king no man can slay." Speculation has been rife about who might become the Witch-king in the show, and this seemed to answer all of those questions… until Pallando dies, anyway. The Witch-king is a dark figure, leader of the Ringwraiths, who is ultimately killed by Eowyn (as seen in The Return of the King). With Pallando ruled out, it once again looks like Theo is the likeliest candidate, especially since he couldn't resist rescuing his ring after Galadriel tried to destroy it in episode 7.

    According to recent reports, nori returns thanks to a vision from Sauron, meant to deceive Gandalf into joining his side. However, Gandalf is able to figure out that he's not really seeing his old friend by referencing her brother. Then, the illusion ends. Later in the episode we catch a glimpse of the real Nori, looking up at the sky, as Gandalf brings Pallando back to the light. It seems she's not been taken by Sauron at all, and may return in the upcoming season 4.

    Recent findings suggest that galadriel threw Theo's ring into a pot of molten metal to free him from its influence in episode 7. However, Theo was unable to walk away, still mesmerized by its power. So, we can assume he retrieved the ring and returned to Sauron's service in between episodes.

    Industry observers note that tom Bombadil makes Pallando's ring disappear, which so impresses Gandalf he offers the other man his hat (which Tom gracefully declines). Just what he has actually done with the ring is unknown for now, since we know for a fact that Sauron will eventually have all nine rings in his power to give to his Ringwraiths.

    In a recent development, since the beginning of the series, there have been ominous signs that Númenor is doomed (as it is in Tolkien's source material). When Sauron surrenders, Pharazôn gloats, while Gil-galad indicates he sees the "doom of men" in the action. In Tolkien's works, Númenor is essentially destroyed as a punishment for hubris, when it invades the Undying Lands, AKA Valinor, to try and take immortality. Pharazôn is certainly showing this kind of doomed arrogance, which Sauron seems to be taking advantage of – indeed, in Tolkien, Sauron manipulates Pharazôn as his prisoner, and it looks like this storyline is coming in season 4, judging by that smirk.

    Sources indicate that sauron receives a letter from Pharazôn gloating that Númenor is the "king of men." It seems the Dark Lord sees some opportunity here, as he immediately goes to surrender to the forces of Númenor and the Elves. While the Elves are wary, Pharazôn is delighted. However, in Tolkien's works, Sauron helps bring about the end of Númenor by manipulating Pharazôn as his prisoner. It looks like this is Sauron's next scheme, signalled by his devious smirk.

    Recent findings suggest that before surrendering, Sauron takes off the One Ring. However, he has most likely concealed it somewhere he can wear it again when he needs it, since we know from Tolkien's work this is not the end of the Dark Lord.

    Yes, Amazon has officially declared that there will be a The Rings of Power season 4. The series is in pre-production now and will begin filming in the UK in spring.

    No, there is no Rings of Power season 3 post-credits scene. Once the episode ends, you're free to turn it off.

    Industry observers note that all episodes of The Rings of Power season 3 are streaming on Prime Video now. For more, check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each update may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

    Coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, new items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This revision will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

    In a recent development, late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major update. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

    Recent findings suggest that last but not least, the planned April update will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

    Are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

    #109394. Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer

    Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A common antibody found throughout the digestive tract may provide an unexpected defense against colon cancer.
    • It has been revealed that in a study published in Nature, scientists found that mice missing a type of antibody known as immunoglobulin A (IgA) developed more than twice as many colon tumors as mice with normal levels of the antibody.
    • Even more promising, when the team administered IgA orally to mice that lacked the antibody, the animals no longer demonstrated an elevated risk of developing tumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A common antibody found throughout the digestive tract may provide an unexpected defense against colon cancer. Researchers at Rockefeller University have discovered that these immune molecules help regulate the growth of cells lining the intestine, potentially preventing the uncontrolled cell division that can lead to tumors.

    It has been revealed that in a study published in Nature, scientists found that mice missing a type of antibody known as immunoglobulin A (IgA) developed more than twice as many colon tumors as mice with normal levels of the antibody. The researchers also uncovered how this protection works. IgA attaches to cells along the intestinal lining and helps prevent them from multiplying too rapidly.

    Even more promising, when the team administered IgA orally to mice that lacked the antibody, the animals no longer demonstrated an elevated risk of developing tumors.

    Sources indicate that "One intriguing aspect of this work is that it reveals how a natural defense in the gut restrains the cell division that can lead to cancer," notes senior author Daniel Mucida, who leads Rockefeller's Laboratory of Mucosal Immunology. "Most cancer research focuses on trying to destroy a tumor that already exists, but what if we could intervene before tumors form?".

    The findings may help explain why people with IgA deficiency, a condition in which the body produces little or none of this antibody, face a greater risk of colorectal cancer. They also offer new insight into how gut bacteria, immune defenses, and intestinal cells work together to influence cancer development, potentially even in people with otherwise healthy immune systems.

    Why the Gut Contains So Much of This Antibody.

    According to recent reports, igA is one of the immune system's most abundant antibodies in the digestive tract, where it provides an notable early defense against potentially harmful microbes. Unlike antibodies that recognize a single specific target, IgA can interact with many different kinds of gut bacteria and even certain healthy cells belonging to the body.

    Scientists have known for decades that the intestines contain unusually large quantities of IgA. However, the reasons for its abundance, and the full range of functions it performs, have remained incompletely understood.

    Mucida's laboratory investigates how the intestine manages two essential but sometimes competing responsibilities. It must defend the body against dangerous microorganisms while allowing nutrients from food to pass into the bloodstream. Earlier research from his team has also helped explain how immune cells in the digestive tract contribute to food intolerances and allergies.

    For the new study, Gregory Donaldson, a former postdoctoral researcher at Rockefeller who is now an assistant professor at UCLA, set out to better understand how IgA interacts with intestinal bacteria and whether those interactions might influence the development of colon cancer.

    "We know these antibodies bind bacteria and, by doing so, can shape the microbiome," he notes. "And because IgA deficiency, which affects about 1 in 500 people in the U.S., is linked to colorectal cancer, I wondered whether these interactions might be relevant to the disease.".

    Recent findings suggest that the microbiome is the community of microorganisms living in and on the body. In the intestines, these microbes perform important functions related to digestion and immune health, but certain bacteria can also contribute to disease under the wrong conditions.

    Missing Gut Antibodies More Than Doubled Colon Tumors.

    In a recent development, to investigate IgA's protective effects, Donaldson compared mice that could not produce the antibody with mice that had normal IgA levels. Both groups were raised together, allowing the researchers to control for differences in food and exposure to microorganisms.

    Recent findings suggest that the results revealed a striking difference. Animals without IgA developed substantially more colorectal tumors than their counterparts, consistent with the increased colorectal cancer risk observed in humans with IgA deficiency.

    Sources indicate that the association was not limited to a single experimental setup. Researchers observed the same pattern using multiple models of colon cancer, strengthening the evidence that IgA plays a meaningful protective role.

    "We found this was true for several different kinds of models of colon cancer, so that was a really convincing effect," notes Donaldson.

    Industry observers note that the team then tested whether replacing the missing antibody could reverse the effect. When mice lacking IgA received oral doses of the antibody, their increased susceptibility to colon tumors disappeared.

    This result suggested that IgA does more than simply accompany other protective processes in the intestine. Its presence appears to directly influence conditions that determine whether tumors develop.

    Scientists Discover a Natural Brake on Cancer Cell Growth.

    Recent findings suggest that to understand the mechanism behind this protection, the researchers examined epithelial cells, which form the inner lining of the intestine. These cells are particularly important because colon cancer begins when cells in this tissue undergo changes that allow them to grow uncontrollably.

    Industry observers note that the intestinal lining is constantly renewing itself. Older or damaged cells are replaced by new ones, making controlled cell division essential for keeping the digestive tract healthy. However, when the signals that regulate this process become disrupted, excessive growth can create opportunities for cancer to develop.

    In a recent development, in mice without IgA, the researchers identified changes in gene activity associated with cell proliferation, the process through which cells divide and increase in number. Crucially, these changes appeared before any tumors became visible, suggesting that the antibody helps regulate an early step in cancer development.

    "We assumed there must be some sort of receptor on the epithelial cells that was mediating this," Donaldson notes.

    The researchers suspected that IgA was interacting with a specific molecular structure on the surface of intestinal cells, allowing it to influence how those cells behaved.

    Gabriella Lima dos Reis, the study's second author and a graduate student working in Gabriel Victora's laboratory, investigated a promising candidate called DMBT1.

    DMBT1 is a receptor found on the surface of epithelial cells that can bind to IgA. Previous research had connected it to several types of cancer, but scientists had not established precisely how it functions in the development of colon tumors.

    How Gut Bacteria and IgA Control Tumor Formation.

    Further experiments revealed that DMBT1 plays two very different roles depending on whether IgA is present.

    When intestinal bacteria are present, DMBT1 activates signals that encourage epithelial cells to divide. This response is part of the normal activity of the intestinal lining, which must continually replace cells to maintain its protective barrier.

    IgA helps keep that growth under control. When the antibody binds to DMBT1, it restrains the receptor's activity, effectively acting as a brake on cell proliferation.

    Without IgA, however, DMBT1 signaling can continue without sufficient restraint. Intestinal cells then divide more rapidly than they should, increasing the likelihood that tumors will develop.

    The researchers confirmed that this excessive growth depends on several interacting factors. When gut bacteria were absent, DMBT1 signaling was disabled, or normal amounts of IgA were available, epithelial cell division remained under control.

    Together, these findings reveal how a common immune molecule helps maintain the delicate balance between necessary tissue renewal and potentially dangerous overgrowth.

    "If IgA is missing, epithelial cells that are performing their normal function -- responding to bacteria by producing new cells -- can keep dividing unchecked, leading to cancer," Mucida says. "We think this homeostatic effect is IgA's main function. This was a substantial surprise.".

    Industry observers note that homeostasis refers to the body's ability to maintain stable, healthy conditions despite constant changes in its environment. In this case, IgA appears to support that balance by preventing normal intestinal cell renewal from becoming excessive.

    A Fresh Possibility for Preventing Colon Cancer.

    By identifying DMBT1's normal role in intestinal cells, the Rockefeller team has uncovered a potential target for future colon cancer prevention strategies.

    Instead of waiting until a tumor develops and then attempting to destroy it, researchers may eventually be able to influence the biological signals that make tumors more likely to form.

    "Based on the mechanism we discovered, perhaps we could influence epithelial cells to be less likely to develop into a tumor," Mucida indicates. "We know, for example, that having polyps increases your chances of getting colon cancer, so we think that there could be an opportunity to target this pathway after polyps are removed. Right now, there are no interventions available at that point.".

    Colon polyps are growths that develop along the inner lining of the large intestine. Although many are harmless, some can eventually become cancerous. Removing them during a colonoscopy can reduce cancer risk, but researchers are interested in finding additional ways to prevent future tumors from developing.

    The newly identified IgA and DMBT1 pathway could offer one such opportunity, although additional research is needed to determine whether targeting it would be effective and safe in humans.

    Could Beneficial Gut Bacteria Help Prevent Cancer?

    The discovery also raises another intriguing possibility. Certain intestinal bacteria may actively help protect against cancer by influencing how epithelial cells behave or by encouraging the production of protective antibodies.

    While much of the research into the gut microbiome and cancer has focused on harmful bacteria that promote tumor formation or accelerate cancer growth, some microbes may have the opposite effect.

    "What is potentially even more exciting is that there is evidence that individual species of bacteria can have really specific effects on epithelial cells as well," Donaldson notes. "A lot of research has focused on bacteria that induce tumors or can exacerbate their growth, but we have some evidence that there are bacteria that could do the opposite, just as IgA does. To that end, perhaps we could develop a probiotic supplement that induces a protective IgA response. This is all very speculative, but it's one direction that we could look towards in the future.".

    Sources indicate that such an approach would aim to use beneficial microorganisms to stimulate the body's existing protective mechanisms rather than directly attacking cancer cells. However, the idea remains speculative, and the mouse experiments do not establish that taking IgA supplements or probiotics can prevent colon cancer in people.

    It has been revealed that for now, the findings provide a clearer picture of how the immune system and gut microbiome cooperate to maintain healthy intestinal tissue. They also suggest that some of the body's most notable defenses against cancer may operate long before the disease becomes detectable.

    Mucida adds, "Overall, there is a lot more to learn about how the dance between bacteria, antibodies, and epithelial cells in the gut works to maintain health.".

    Industry observers note that materials provided by Rockefeller University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Halloween has ended, making way for jollier celebrations and bigger gifts.
    • Patch 1.3.5.0 for Escape From Tarkov marks the end of its traditional Halloween event, which means Scav violence is back to its normal levels.
    • The highlight of the enhancement is on the performance side, where Battlestate Games has unlocked improved frames across the board, thanks in part to an engine upgrade that finally brings Escape From Tarkov to current-gen standards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Halloween has ended, making way for jollier celebrations and bigger gifts. In the communal spirit of Thanksgiving week, which is absolutely not a thing in Russia, Escape from Tarkov has dropped one of its biggest updates since its 1.0 launch last year.

    Patch 1.3.5.0 for Escape From Tarkov marks the end of its traditional Halloween event, which means Scav violence is back to its normal levels.

    The highlight of the enhancement is on the performance side, where Battlestate Games has unlocked improved frames across the board, thanks in part to an engine upgrade that finally brings Escape From Tarkov to current-gen standards.

    One of the biggest complaints that has plagued Escape From Tarkov, especially after the 1.0 launch, was loading times. When playing online, loading the map and assets and actually connecting to a server were done in tandem. The practical outcome was that you'd often spend 5, sometimes even 10 minutes or more staring at a screen.

    Starting with patch 1.3.5.0, Escape From Tarkov now does the asset buffering and server matchmaking in parallel, shaving some precious minutes off of the loading screen.

    Recent findings suggest that to help longer playing sessions feel smoother, the game now cleans up after itself better at the end of each raid. This will have a particularly tangible impact for consumers who aren't hogging up 32GB of RAM instead of sharing it with poor Sam Altman. On top of that, the challenges where uncontrolled RAM usage could happen during long gaming sessions have finally been fixed.

    Game server performance has also undergone an optimization pass. The practical implication here is that you'll have to deal with less hitreg and packet loss complications. Besides ghost shots, doors will now work properly, removing certain errors where they collide with the player in a jumbled case between the client and server.

    In a recent development, as part of the new 1.3.5.0 patch, the game has unified its graphics rendering engine under RenderStack. Most of the big improvements from this change are yet to come, but RenderStack lays the groundwork for the future of the game while already giving players some performance bonuses.

    Sources indicate that vegetation and long-distance rendering have a new distant projection system, resulting in better graphics for trees, bushes, and other parts of nature while you do your run. This is especially noticeable in the Shoreline and Woods maps, where you spend most of your time breathing in the crisp forest air. Seasonal transitions will now work with preloading landscape materials to significantly reduce RAM usage.

    Recent findings suggest that lighting and shadow transitions will now be smoother, resulting in less strain on the CPU and GPU while the game is running. When staring down magnifying optics, you have fewer frame drops and a crisper image, especially when running upscalers like DLSS or FSR.

    In the future, the change to RenderStack will allow Tarkov to use DLSS Frame Generation and FSR 4.0.

    It will allow Tarkov to use NVIDIA DLSS technology and FSR 2 and FSR 3.

    If a player happens to lose connection during a raid due to network problems, it will now be easier and faster to join back up. With the upcoming addition, the game won’t need to reload the entire map, resources, or world state, as it will only require the connection to come back, and you’ll be joined back up with everything else stored where it was left off.

    These changes won’t be implemented when the game client closes unexpectedly, such as OS failure, PC restart, and similar changes.

    To celebrate, Escape From Tarkov is holding discounts on cosmetic packs in the Expansion Hub of the game for each of the factions, such as the USEC Veteran Pack, BEAR Veteran Pack, PMC Veteran Pack, and an Executive PMC Pack.

    Escape from Tarkov is available for Windows via Steam and the official Escape from Tarkov website.

    It has been revealed that nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik. The move follows an eighth-place 2026 for the club and comes days after BLG ended Korea's four-year hold on the World Championship.

    Industry observers note that kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November. The club used its official social media channels to make the announcement. Deft began his military service after the 2024 season ended.

    Sources indicate that the deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship. Jungler Hong ‘Pyosik’ Chang-hyeon joined later the same day, alongside support Moon ‘Andil’ Gwan-bin. Top laner Hwang ‘Kingen’ Seong-hoon had re-signed a day earlier.

    Deft’s signing was announced at 7pm. The Pyosik and Andil additions that followed completed Nongshim’s five-man starting line-up, Inven Global reported. Mid laner Seon ‘Calix’ Hyeon-bin provides continuity. He has been with the organisation since 2021 and extended his deal on 18 November.

    Deft brings a long winning record. He made his debut with MVP Blue in 2013. His titles include the LCK, the LPL, the Mid-Season Invitational and the 2022 World Championship.

    Kingen first joined Nongshim for the 2025 season. Pyosik arrives after a difficult 2026 at DN SOOPers. That team lost a run of matches, and rookie Sharvel took his starting place.

    The move had been signalled. About a month before the announcement, Sheep Esports reported from Korean sources that Nongshim planned to sign Deft. The same report stated rookie AD carry Diable would need a newly introduced team.

    The signings mark a sharp change of direction after a poor year. Once the league campaign was over, the team lasted just a single match in the play-ins.

    The deal lands days after a setback for the whole league. Bilibili Gaming’s victory over Gen.G came at the Barclays Center in Fresh York. It gave the organisation its first Summoner’s Cup.

    BLG won all four of its series against LCK teams at the tournament. Every LCK seed fell to the Chinese side on its way to the trophy. The title is also the LPL’s first since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

    'Deft' has signed a contract as the newly introduced ADC of NS RedForce LCK Team.

    Please look forward to and support Deft, who has written newly introduced history with an unbreakable spirit through countless trials, as he takes on new challenges and delivers great… pic.twitter.com/bHa1uJWwKV.

    — NS RedForce (@NS_RedForce) November 19, 2026.

    According to recent reports, for Nongshim, a line-up built around three 2022 champions now has an international calendar to aim at. Riot Games has moved First Stand 2027 from Southeast Asia to China and renamed it First Stand: All In. It will be a one-off expanded edition with more teams and players.

    Industry observers note that spain gets its debut as a Mid-Season Invitational host in 2027, with Valencia’s Feria de Valencia as the venue. Before that, Riot prepares to publish First Stand: All In’s format and qualification process in January.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

    Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

    The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

    That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

    In a recent development, the gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet newly introduced characters.

    Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

    Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

    Recent findings suggest that the game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

    In a recent development, you can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game introduces. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A substantial part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit.
    • According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Latest Game+!" a post from the devs explains.
    • It has been revealed that in any case, the enhancement goes a tad further than that.

    A substantial part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 enhancement next week that adds in a new game plus mode.

    According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Latest Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

    It has been revealed that in any case, the enhancement goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

    Industry observers note that overall, a bit of a smaller patch compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something notable or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

    GTA 6: Where to Find Cave Diving

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, ​There feels like endless activities to do in Grand Theft Auto 6.
    • In a recent development, most of the side activities are hidden, not properly introduced or shown on the map where to find them, and that’s exactly the case for cave diving.
    • Recent findings suggest that the cave system isn’t too far off from where you start in chapter 2 of the story.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, ​There feels like endless activities to do in Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether it’s racing through the streets of Vice City, playing mini-golf with your loved one or robbing banks, there’s no shortage of things to do in this vast open world adventure.

    In a recent development, most of the side activities are hidden, not properly introduced or shown on the map where to find them, and that’s exactly the case for cave diving. This dangerous and claustrophobic activity might not be for everyone, but it certainly can yield you some good rewards if you decide to bring Jason or Lucia down.

    Recent findings suggest that the cave system isn’t too far off from where you start in chapter 2 of the story. You will be able to access it in the first chapter, but it will be a bit of a drive. This is located all the way in Kelly County. This can be found in the western portion of the map.

    The best way to find where you’re going is right in-between the L and E on the Leonida text if you zoom all the way out on the map. You will see a rather large network of swamps and rivers called the Emerald Springs. Here, you will want to go directly west of the “Emerald Springs” text on the map, around the rivers and on the western side.

    There will be a small hut area on the map that branches off from the road, and this will lead to Selkie Hole. The Selkie is a mythological creature from Norse and Celtic lore. Up here, you will spot various divers and a couple of them just leave their scuba gear out there. Grab them (they won’t care) and head inside the cave through the chain-link door. Down the stairs is the cave system. Happy exploring!

    A light illuminates rocks in a dark underwater cave, with an Explorer’s Knife prompt on screen.

    Sadly, most of the cave system is already mapped – literally. You’ll be able to open up your in-game map and see just how far the tunnels go, and that’s all there is. Now, we say “that’s all there is”, but in reality, it’s a surprisingly lengthy and sprawling system that will take quite a bit to fully explore.

    Because of that, there will be some hidden items spread throughout. One of the most common items in this cave system is Meteorites. These are unique items spread throughout the open world in which you’ll be able to pawn for some extra cash, usually for quite a bit (especially early on). It’s the same as collectibles such as cards and doubloons, but yielding the most trade value.

    On top of that, you will find other unique items such as an Explorer’s Knife pretty close to the entrance of the cave system. It’s nothing too special but one that you will always have considering it’s a legendary weapon.

    Tech Report: Scientists discover a fresh type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (989 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants.
    • Recent findings suggest that the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression.
    • Recent findings suggest that circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

    Recent findings suggest that the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, showed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.

    Recent findings suggest that circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.

    Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.

    A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied.

    It has been revealed that to investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.

    Sources indicate that the researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.

    According to recent reports, those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.

    In a recent development, the differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.

    First author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:.

    "Our research has identified circadian depression as a new subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.

    "Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them.".

    Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective.

    One of the most important implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.

    It has been revealed that medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.

    Recent findings suggest that however, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.

    In a recent development, because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.

    Industry observers note that co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:.

    "Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.

    "For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is crucial to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances.".

    A New Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People.

    Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially important for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.

    Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.

    The findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.

    By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.

    "We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.

    "Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition.".

    Sources indicate that materials provided by University of Sydney. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.
    • The two newly introduced features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17.
    • The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis unveiled The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

    The two newly introduced features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

    The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

    Industry observers note that created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature releases, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

    Alongside this, the game is also introducing a upcoming virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

    It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

    In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

    Recent findings suggest that in the blog post announcing the newly introduced features, Maxis stated that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

    You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Live service games have it rough in the current gaming industry, forced to fight tooth and nail against half a dozen well-established titles that have all but consumed the worthwhile player base.
    • Industry observers note that some, like Capcom’s Exoprimal, try to throw everything at the wall to see what sticks with players, and I can’t lie, mech suits vs dinosaurs was a compelling first pitch.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Live service games have it rough in the current gaming industry, forced to fight tooth and nail against half a dozen well-established titles that have all but consumed the worthwhile player base. Anyone new on the block needs to really justify their airtime, and for many, it’s simply not worth the hassle of getting torn apart by consumers.

    Industry observers note that some, like Capcom’s Exoprimal, try to throw everything at the wall to see what sticks with players, and I can’t lie, mech suits vs dinosaurs was a compelling first pitch. After three solid years of support, however, Exoprimal is facing End of Service, just announced by Capcom.

    Marked for death after September 2027, players have less than a year to enjoy their Jurassic jungle gym.

    Exoprimal was an odd title, announced back in 2022 and released in July of 2023. One of Capcom's few big-budget standalone titles, surrounded by its long-running franchises, Exoprimal was Capcom’s attempt to leap into the third-person shooter live-service genre dominated by Warframe.

    Exoprimal itself found a niche audience that enjoyed what was on offer, with a humble but positive review on Steam to this day. Despite the receptive crowd, players were disappointed by the lack of content on launch, leaving them with plenty of hunger for more dino-killing, mech-fueled action.

    Sources indicate that capcom eventually relented in a series of effective but spaced-out patches, leaving players feeling like the second fiddle as the company continued to focus on its heavy hitters. The End of Service announcement is a genuine death sentence for a title like Exoprimal, not just revealing an end to active development, but a date the game will be simply unplayable after.

    Recent findings suggest that the announcement is unfortunate, but sadly not at all unexpected. When compared to other middling live service ventures, Exoprimal managing a total of 4 years of support is on the higher end. This, sadly, just means players who put in the time are left in the dust, at least until they find a third-party way to keep playing.

    Anyone fresh on the block needs to really justify their airtime, and for many, it’s simply not worth the hassle of getting torn apart by consumers.

    Industry observers note that modders have been the absolute team players when it comes to keeping the lights on for live service communities, and Exoprimal is no different. If they can’t, Exoprimal is facing downright elimination, a sad sight for one of Capcom’s most video-gamey upcoming titles that could absolutely have made it in the long haul.

    In a recent development, end-of-Service announcements have killed tons of games, both strong and weak. It’s been a major hit to the industry, with half of the recent releases that drop threatened by an eventual death knell. Any investment in a title that isn’t guaranteed to succeed, like massive franchise sequels, feels like a gamble, and it can be absolutely exhausting.

    Sources indicate that capcom is one tech giant that can absolutely afford to put out smaller, standalone titles to make some cash and potentially introduce whole upcoming franchises. Pragmata is one such gem, a fantastic little puzzle shooter that came out of nowhere. A perfect little bite-sized adventure is perfectly Capcom, and their care for anything other than Monster Hunter shows they just truly aren’t great with long-term support.

    According to recent reports, compared to Monster Hunter, with its constant latest hunts, events, and short-term content to keep players engaged over time, all the while hyping a massive expansion just over the horizon. Exoprimal struggled to offer anything beyond cosmetics and microtransactions for short-term content between missions, making it clear the small team working on the title didn’t get much focus.

    Sadly, Exoprimal’s cancellation isn't surprising, but the fanbase isn’t going anywhere. They may be small, but they’ve got the passion and effort to try and keep the party going, at least for a while longer.

    #109377. Breaking: Fresh gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1148 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Fresh gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1148 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Researchers in Japan have developed a promising new treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed.
    • Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light.
    • Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Researchers in Japan have developed a promising new treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed. Unlike conventional approaches that can eliminate both good and bad bacteria, the new therapy is designed to target specific microbes responsible for damaging gums and the bone that supports teeth.

    Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light. Early experiments in human cell cultures and mice suggest that it could offer a more precise way to combat periodontitis, a serious form of gum disease that can eventually lead to tooth loss. The findings were published in the Journal of Translational Medicine.

    Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.

    According to recent reports, the human mouth contains a complex community of microorganisms, many of which play important roles in maintaining oral health. Problems can arise when harmful bacteria multiply and disturb this delicate balance.

    Sources indicate that one particularly troublesome species is Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis), which scientists classify as a keystone pathogen. This means it can have an outsized influence on the surrounding microbial community, even when it is not especially abundant. By promoting inflammation and disrupting the normal balance of oral bacteria, it can contribute to the destruction of the bone that holds teeth in place.

    Treating periodontitis often involves eliminating the bacteria responsible for the infection. However, some existing antimicrobial treatments do not distinguish between harmful organisms and microbes that help maintain a healthy mouth.

    "Current treatments for periodontitis, including antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT), eliminate both pathogenic and beneficial oral bacteria," said Kazuhide Sato, one of the corresponding authors and a lecturer at Nagoya University. "These approaches often disrupt the entire oral microbial ecosystem and can also release lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an endotoxin that may exacerbate inflammation.".

    Scientists Adapt Cancer Therapy to Target Gum Disease Bacteria.

    To overcome these limitations, the Nagoya University team turned to a technology originally designed to treat cancer. Known as near-infrared photoimmunotherapy, it uses antibodies linked to a light-sensitive dye to recognize specific targets. Once the compound attaches to its intended target, exposure to near-infrared light activates the dye and produces a damaging effect.

    Recent findings suggest that the researchers adapted this strategy to attack P. gingivalis without unnecessarily disturbing other oral bacteria. Their approach relies on IgY, a type of antibody collected from the egg yolks of hens that have been immunized against the pathogen.

    Egg yolk antibodies offer a practical advantage because they can be produced in large quantities at relatively low cost. This could make them an attractive option for developing targeted treatments that are affordable and scalable.

    The resulting technology, called near-infrared photo-antibacterial targeting therapy (NIR-PAT²), was developed by researchers at Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine. The team included first author Hiroshi Maruyama, Professor Hideharu Hibi, and corresponding authors Sato and Kiyoshi Sakai.

    To determine whether the treatment could destroy harmful bacteria while protecting healthy tissue, the researchers tested it in human cell cultures and mice. They also compared its effects with those of conventional antimicrobial therapies.

    Light-Activated Antibodies Destroy Harmful Bacteria.

    In a recent development, laboratory experiments demonstrated that the antibody and dye combination attached specifically to P. gingivalis. Other bacterial species and healthy human gum cells were left unaffected.

    When the researchers illuminated the targeted bacteria with near-infrared light, the activated dye damaged their outer membranes, ultimately killing them.

    It has been revealed that microscopic examination revealed an key difference between this technique and conventional antimicrobial light therapy. Bacteria exposed to the upcoming treatment developed tiny openings in their membranes but largely maintained their overall shape. By contrast, conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy caused the bacteria to break apart completely.

    It has been revealed that the distinction matters because destroying bacterial cells can release substances that contribute to inflammation. Preserving the overall structure of the targeted bacteria, even after killing them, could help limit this unwanted effect.

    The researchers also examined how the treatments affected healthy human gum cells. Their targeted therapy caused no detectable harm to these cells, while conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy produced cellular damage and slowed healing.

    New Treatment Reduces Bone Loss in Mice.

    The team next investigated whether these laboratory findings would translate into meaningful improvements in gum disease.

    In mice with periodontitis, the experimental therapy significantly reduced the loss of alveolar bone, the part of the jawbone that surrounds and supports teeth. Preventing this type of bone deterioration is especially important because advanced periodontitis can loosen teeth and eventually cause them to fall out.

    Analysis of the animals' saliva revealed another encouraging result. The treatment reduced P. gingivalis while preserving beneficial Streptococcus bacteria, helping maintain a healthier balance of microorganisms in the mouth.

    Conventional antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, on the other hand, eliminated both harmful and beneficial bacteria in the experiments, causing broader disruption to the oral microbial community.

    "Results demonstrated that, unlike antibiotics or standard light therapy, this approach selectively removes the primary pathogenic species while preserving the remainder of the oral bacterial community," Sato said.

    Together, the findings suggest that targeting individual disease-causing bacteria could help control gum disease while avoiding some of the unintended consequences of broader antimicrobial treatments.

    AI Could Help Develop More Precise Gum Disease Treatments.

    According to recent reports, although the early results are promising, the researchers recognize that periodontitis is a complex disease involving multiple bacterial species. Eliminating P. gingivalis alone may not be sufficient to treat every case.

    To address this challenge, the team plans to use artificial intelligence (AI) to examine publicly available information about oral bacteria. By identifying other key microorganisms and studying how different species interact, they hope to uncover additional targets for future therapies.

    The researchers also see potential implications beyond oral health. Periodontitis has been linked to several other medical conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes.

    Understanding the relationships between oral bacteria and these conditions could eventually help scientists identify which patients are most likely to benefit from specific treatments. AI analysis may play a role in making those decisions and guiding the development of more personalized approaches to gum disease.

    In a recent development, for now, the therapy remains experimental, with its effectiveness demonstrated in laboratory studies and mice rather than human clinical trials. However, the findings point toward a possible future in which treating gum disease means selectively removing harmful bacteria instead of disrupting the entire microbial community that helps keep the mouth healthy.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports.
    • The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10 UTC on Saturday 21 November, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.
    • Sources indicate that the result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

    The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10 UTC on Saturday 21 November, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

    Sources indicate that the result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that mentioned it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

    Industry observers note that the Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

    Industry observers note that shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

    Across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

    The organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

    The prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

    When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a fresh interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

    It has been revealed that "Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a new interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

    I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

    It has been revealed that in any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

    IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes.
    • Recent findings suggest that the achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage.
    • According to recent reports, in their new paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes. Perhaps even more significantly, researchers were able to establish statistical confidence in the accuracy of the quantum computer's results, addressing one of the biggest obstacles in the field.

    Recent findings suggest that the achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage. This milestone occurs when a quantum computer performs a computational task beyond the practical capabilities of leading classical computing methods while producing results that can be trusted.

    According to recent reports, in their new paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits. The experiment represents one of the largest demonstrations of logical quantum computing to date. The researchers have also made their circuits and experimental results publicly available through the Quantum Advantage Tracker.

    Solving Quantum Computing's Verification Problem.

    Unlike conventional computers, which process information using bits that represent either zero or one, quantum computers rely on quantum bits, or qubits. These can exist in combinations of both states and interact through a phenomenon known as quantum entanglement. These properties allow quantum computers to approach certain computational problems in fundamentally different ways.

    Sources indicate that for years, scientists have tested the capabilities of quantum computers using a benchmark called random circuit sampling (RCS). This technique involves running a series of randomly selected quantum operations and generating samples from a complex probability distribution. As the circuits grow larger and more complicated, reproducing their output with a classical computer becomes increasingly difficult.

    According to recent reports, however, this approach creates a fundamental dilemma. If a computation is too difficult for a classical computer to reproduce, how can researchers establish that the quantum computer performed it correctly?

    As computational complexity increases, independently verifying the results becomes progressively more difficult and eventually impractical without making strong assumptions about how accurately the quantum hardware operates.

    In a recent development, to overcome this problem, the IBM and University of Chicago team developed a more structured alternative to random circuit sampling. The researchers mathematically demonstrated that their approach preserves the same computational hardness criteria as conventional RCS while introducing a structure that allows errors to be detected during the computation.

    In a recent development, "Verification remains one of the biggest challenges in firmly establishing experimental quantum advantage," stated Bill Fefferman, Associate Professor at the University of Chicago. "This experiment develops techniques to better characterize the fidelity of hard quantum states under noise, increasing confidence that the quantum computer is solving a computationally hard problem.".

    Soumik Ghosh, PhD student in Fefferman's group at the University of Chicago, added, "Beyond strengthening experimental validation, advances in verification have the potential to unlock practical applications for the next generation of quantum computers.".

    70 Logical Qubits and Tenfold Lower Error Rates.

    In a recent development, one of the greatest challenges in building powerful quantum computers is their extraordinary sensitivity to errors. Quantum information can be disrupted by environmental disturbances, imperfections in hardware, and inaccuracies in the operations used to manipulate qubits. As computations become longer and more complex, these errors can accumulate and undermine the reliability of the results.

    Quantum error correction addresses this weakness by encoding quantum information across multiple physical qubits to create more reliable units known as logical qubits. This approach allows certain errors to be identified and, depending on the technique, corrected or accounted for without destroying the underlying quantum information.

    In one of the largest known demonstrations of quantum error correction, the researchers performed computations using 70 protected logical qubits. The experiment involved 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 logical "T gates.".

    Quantum gates are the fundamental operations that manipulate quantum information, much like logic gates in conventional computers. Two-qubit gates allow qubits to interact, while T gates enable additional types of quantum operations needed for universal quantum computing. Together, these gate counts illustrate the considerable complexity of the experiment.

    It has been revealed that by encoding the quantum circuits, the researchers achieved effective logical error rates 10 times lower than the underlying physical error rates. This substantial reduction allowed the quantum computer to maintain remarkably high fidelity, a measure of how closely the actual quantum state matches the intended one, despite performing thousands of complex operations.

    According to recent reports, "We are now firmly in the quantum advantage era," said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. "We have demonstrated a quantum computation beyond the practical reach of classical computers that establishes, with statistical confidence, a lower bound on how faithfully it was executed. This milestone gives scientists, developers, and businesses a new foundation for trusting quantum computers as they scale to problems far beyond what we can achieve classically.".

    The researchers found that many leading classical simulation techniques would require impractically long periods to reproduce the computation. IBM's quantum computer, by comparison, accomplished the task in approximately 15 minutes.

    Although the experiment was designed to demonstrate quantum advantage rather than solve an immediate real-world problem, it addresses two essential requirements for making large-scale quantum computing practical: controlling errors and establishing confidence in computational results.

    By demonstrating both capabilities in a computation beyond the practical reach of leading classical methods, the researchers have taken a significant step toward a future in which quantum computers could reliably tackle scientific and industrial problems that are right now out of reach.
