    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Capcom has announced that its dinosaur shooter Exoprimal will be unplayable next September as the servers are being taken offline.

    While not quite as massive as the year it had in 2026, Capcom's 2023 was incredible, with Resident Evil 4 and Street Fighter 6 releasing as two certified game of the year contenders and as two of the all-time greats in their respective genres. But there was another, namely Exoprimal, a PvPvE shooter where you took a ton of Overwatch-like character classes into brawls where you'd fend off armies of dinosaurs.

    According to recent reports, it had a bit of a cult following, but Capcom has unveiled it'll be joining the pile of dead live service titles next year. In a post on the Exoprimal website, Capcom confirms that services for the game will go offline on September 29, 2027, with the post reading, "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

    In a recent development, as it begins the shutdown process, the game's survival pass premium tiers (aka, the paid battle pass) have been removed from the in-game store already. The game itself will be taken off sale on March 30, 2027, and those who own it will have six more months to play it before it's gone forever. With no way to access the content in single-player, it'll sadly join the ever-growing list of games that are just gone, which certainly isn't a bad omen for the all-digital future.

    Recent findings suggest that exoprimal was perhaps best known for being the bane of many a Dino Crisis fan upon its announcement – especially when there's a character who looks like that game's heroine Regina, who featured heavily in marketing. It was genuinely a fun time when you got into it, but it suffered from the same fate many live services do, that being there's too damn many of them, so it never really took off. It also didn't help that Exoprimal's best content was hidden behind a ton of playtime.

    Dino Crisis is more than "Resident Evil with dinosaurs" – it shaped survival horror as we know it.

    "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

    It has been revealed that since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

    #109343. Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1180 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

    Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Adults age 65 and older who have dementia or other cognitive disorders are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of medications used to treat anxiety, sleep disturbances, psychosis, and other conditions affecting the central nervous system.
    • Potential consequences include more emergency room visits, longer and more frequent hospital stays, declining mental health, and an increased risk of premature death.
    • New research from the University at Buffalo (UB) offers some encouraging news, however.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Adults age 65 and older who have dementia or other cognitive disorders are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of medications used to treat anxiety, sleep disturbances, psychosis, and other conditions affecting the central nervous system.

    Potential consequences include more emergency room visits, longer and more frequent hospital stays, declining mental health, and an increased risk of premature death.

    New research from the University at Buffalo (UB) offers some encouraging news, however. Between 2011 and 2022, the proportion of older adults with cognitive disorders taking medications that could impair their cognitive function decreased significantly.

    After analyzing data from 2,796 older adults with cognitive disorders who lived independently, researchers found that exposure to potentially inappropriate medications fell from 39.3% in 2011 to 29.3% in 2022.

    According to recent reports, "This is a population with some mental issues that relate to the central nervous system. These drugs also act on the central nervous system, so they can be too much for older adults if inappropriately used," claims Haowen Hsu, PharmD, a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Pharmacy Practice at the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences and first author of the study, published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society.

    Reducing the Risks of Common Prescription Drugs.

    According to recent reports, older adults who have spent years taking benzodiazepines such as Xanax for anxiety or sleep medications such as Ambien may benefit from a medically supervised reduction in dosage or gradual discontinuation. These medications can negatively affect cognitive function, balance, and coordination.

    "A central word for patients in this age group is 'deprescribing,' which means, for example, removing inappropriate medications and decreasing the frequency or the dosage. In some cases, it means replacing the current medication with a milder alternative," Hsu indicates. "This is why it's so notable for health care providers to work closely with community pharmacists and homecare nurses to optimize medication safety.".

    To identify potentially problematic drugs, the research team consulted the American Geriatrics Society's Beers Criteria, which identifies approximately 100 medications that may pose risks to older adults. The researchers then concentrated specifically on medications that could present additional dangers for people with diagnosed cognitive disorders.

    According to recent reports, using data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, the team examined a sample representing approximately 29.7 million older Americans with cognitive disorders over the period from 2011 to 2022. They compared individuals prescribed at least one potentially inappropriate medication with those who had not received any of these drugs.

    Medication Safety Has Improved, but Risks Remain.

    Industry observers note that although the study did not examine what caused the decline in exposure to potentially harmful medications, Hsu points to growing awareness among researchers and clinicians over the past two decades. The gradual but sustained improvement may reflect broader advances in geriatric medicine and efforts to make prescription drug use safer.

    It has been revealed that "We were happy to see the percentages of harm decline over that 11-year period," he indicates. "However, one-third of our target population is still exposed to these harmful medications, which isn't good.".

    Older adults, even those without cognitive disorders, are particularly susceptible to harmful drug interactions and inappropriate prescriptions. In some cases, these complications can increase the risk of death. These dangers are a central focus of Team Alice, an ongoing interdisciplinary research initiative at the University at Buffalo dedicated to medication safety.

    A Preventable Death Inspires Change.

    Team Alice takes its name from Alice Brennan, who died in 2009 following a prescription for a muscle relaxant identified as potentially inappropriate under the Beers Criteria. The prescribing error went unrecognized within the health care system, and Brennan died following six weeks of preventable complications.

    Her daughter, Mary Brennan-Taylor, shared her mother's experience with University at Buffalo researchers in the hope of bringing about systemic changes that would spare other patients and families from similar harm.

    Hsu began the fresh study shortly after joining the university's pharmacy school and Team Alice, where he works in the UB Patient Safety Learning Laboratory.

    "This work extends a series of national analyses our group has published on potentially inappropriate medications, quality of life, and health care use in older adults," says David Jacobs, PharmD, PhD, associate professor of pharmacy practice and a principal investigator on Team Alice.

    According to recent reports, "It is especially crucial as older adults with cognitive disorders are the least able to tolerate medications that worsen memory or thinking, yet nearly one in three are still receiving them. Most of these patients have a regular source of care so these medications can be identified and addressed with their care team.".

    Improving Medication Safety for Older Adults.

    Other contributors to the study included Team Alice's fellow principal investigators Ranjit Singh, MD, associate professor and interim chair of the Department of Family Medicine at UB's Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, and Robert Wahler, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice.

    Collin Clark, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice, and Steven Feuerstein, an information systems analyst at the Jacobs School, also contributed to the research.

    The findings underscore the value of thorough medication reviews during routine outpatient appointments. The researchers also suggest incorporating clinical assessment tools such as the Drug Burden Index into acute and outpatient care. Such tools can help health care professionals assess the combined effects of medications that act on the central nervous system and potentially prevent avoidable complications.

    Further research is needed to establish whether improving medication use can enhance quality of life and reduce hospital admissions and emergency room visits among older adults experiencing cognitive difficulties.

    A Rapidly Aging Population Raises Newly introduced Concerns.

    According to recent reports, the findings arrive at a significant moment in global demographic history. According to a recent report from the U.S. Census Bureau, adults age 65 and older now outnumber children from birth through age 5 worldwide for the first time in human history.

    According to recent reports, however, greater longevity does not necessarily translate into more years of good health. The same report indicates that nearly 75% of adults age 65 and older have at least two chronic health conditions. Managing multiple illnesses often requires taking more medications, some of which may have detrimental effects on the aging body and brain.

    Recent findings suggest that "This is an issue that has been building for decades, but the growth of the older adult population has arrived sooner than we expected," Hsu notes. "This means that health care professionals need to pay closer attention than ever to medication safety, especially for older adults experiencing cognitive decline or other complex health concerns.".

    Tech Report: GTA 6's Collectible Trading Cards Are Getting A Real-Life Release This December

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, it's been less than a week since Grand Theft Auto 6 came out, and Rockstar Games has already found another way to get us to spend money on the game.
    • This goes beyond your usual video game merchandise featuring the main characters.
    • According to recent reports, panini America declared its partnership with Rockstar Games on November 24.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, it's been less than a week since Grand Theft Auto 6 came out, and Rockstar Games has already found another way to get us to spend money on the game. If you've been collecting sports cards while exploring Leonida, you'll soon be able to do the same outside the game. Rockstar has partnered with Panini America to bring these fictional sports trading cards to life, and they'll be out in December 2026.

    This goes beyond your usual video game merchandise featuring the main characters. The cards are based on collectibles that actually exist within GTA 6's world, so you might recognize some of the athletes and teams when you open a pack. And if you're hoping to get your hands on some of the rarer cards, there are even a few that are limited to a single copy each.

    According to recent reports, panini America declared its partnership with Rockstar Games on November 24. The officially licensed set is called the GTA VI: Sports Trading Card Collection, and it'll be the first trading card collaboration between the two companies.

    Recent findings suggest that if you've ever collected football or basketball cards, chances are you're already familiar with Panini. They're also known for reprinting comics in Europe, and I still have a copy of the X-Men: The Last Stand Annual 2007 published by Panini Books.

    It has been revealed that what's different this time is that instead of collecting cards featuring actual sports stars, you'll be collecting ones based on athletes from Rockstar's fictional universe. The promotional artwork reveals a mixture of illustrated cards and ones featuring character renders, much like those found in the game itself.

    Industry observers note that the cards will come in boxes containing four packs each. Panini notes a box will typically include two Rookie cards, a Retro card, an Illustrated card and four Special Silvers. These are average figures rather than guaranteed contents for every box.

    There'll also be different colored variants of the cards, including silver, pink, teal and light blue, along with team-colored parallels. The rarest variants have much smaller print runs. The Legend Bronze cards are numbered out of 49, the numbered Silver variants out of 25, and the Gold variants are one-of-a-kind cards.

    Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn’t be surprised if some of the rare cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

    Industry observers note that getting your hands on every variant, however, could be quite a challenge. Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn't be surprised if some of the rarer cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

    In a recent development, even if you don't care about the numbered cards, there's some appeal in having the regular ones. GTA's fictional athletes aren't exactly household names like the ones you'd find in Panini's other sports collections, but you can actually go looking for their cards in Leonida while playing the game.

    Rockstar has been selling GTA merchandise for years, but this particular collaboration reminds me of the sort of extras that used to come with physical copies of video games. The maps that came with older GTA titles, for instance, were something you could actually use while playing and keep long after you were done with the game.

    According to recent reports, ironically, GTA 6's boxed edition doesn't even come with a game disc. So it's nice to see Rockstar making something physical that draws directly from the game rather than simply putting its logo on another piece of merchandise.

    Recent findings suggest that rockstar could've easily gone with a conventional trading card set featuring Jason, Lucia, and other major characters. Instead, it's making replicas of things you might stumble across while taking a break from the story. I'd love to see Rockstar do something similar with other fictional brands from the series, like Sprunk or eCola.

    Unfortunately, Panini hasn't revealed an exact release date, pricing, or which countries the cards will be available in.

    Depending on when the cards go on sale in December, they could make for a pretty good Christmas gift for a GTA fan.
